Definition: to be (causatively, make or act) circumspect and hence, intelligent
BiblicalUsage: Sekal is considering, looking with understanding, and Daniel uses it on the horns: I considered the horns, and behold, there came up among them another little horn, before whom three of the first horns were plucked up by the roots.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe considering is the prophet's work — to look steadily at what is rising, and see the little horn for what it is.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
